## Natural history notes

A native perennial wildflower in the sunflower family, characterized by upright flowering stems, narrow leaves often clustered along the lower portions of the stem, and dense spikes of bright purple flower heads. Clusterleaf Blazing Star occurs primarily in dry, sandy habitats of Florida, including scrub, sandhill, and open pine communities. It is adapted to full sun, well-drained nutrient-poor soils, and periodic fire, which helps maintain the open conditions it requires. Its late-summer to fall flowers provide nectar for butterflies, bees, and other pollinating insects.
